zh.title: 空中巴士公佈2026上半年財報 第二季淨利大增126%
zh.summary: 空中巴士公佈2026年第二季與上半年財務報告。受惠於第二季交機量顯著回升至237架，該季淨利同比大增126%至16.6億美元。累計上半年共交付351架民航機，合併營收達332億歐元。公司重申全年交付約870架飛機的目標，並持續推進客機產能提升計劃。
body: 根據空中巴士與航太媒體《AeroTime》報導，空中巴士於2026年7月29日公佈了2026年上半年的合併財務業績。其中，第二季的財務數字表現尤為亮眼，受惠於民航機交付量的強勁增長，空中巴士在截至2026年6月30日的三個月內，單季淨利同比大幅增長126%，自去年同期的8.42億美元（約合7.32億歐元）增至16.6億美元（約合1.65億歐元），同時該季營收也實現了28%的增長。
在交機表現方面，空中巴士於2026年第二季（4月至6月）向客戶交付了237架民航機，相較於第一季（1月至3月）僅交付的114架大幅攀升。這使得2026年上半年的民航機交付總量達到351架（去年同期為306架），其中包括44架A220、271架A320系列、10架A330以及26架A350客機。
財務表現上，2026年上半年合併營收同比增長12%至332億歐元（約382億美元）；調整後息稅前利潤（EBIT Adjusted）則達到27.27億歐元（去年同期為22.04億歐元）。空中巴士執行長 Guillaume Faury 表示，良好的上半年業績主要反映了民航機交付量的提升，以及國防與航太部門的強勁表現。
在訂單與積壓方面，空中巴士在2026年上半年共錄得886架民航機的新增總訂單（扣除取消後的淨訂單為821架），顯著高於去年同期的494架。截至2026年6月底，空中巴士的民航機未交付訂單（backlog）累積已達9,222架。
展望未來，空中巴士重申其在2026年交付約870架民航機的目標保持不變，並預計全年調整後息稅前利潤（EBIT Adjusted）將達到75億歐元（約86億美元）。同時，各客機項目的產能提升計劃仍持續推進，包括目標在2028年將A220的月產量提升至13架，在2027年底前將A320系列月產量提升至70至75架，並預期在2029年將A330月產量提升至5架、2028年將A350月產量提升至12架。

en.title: Airbus Q2 Profits Surge 126% on Strong Commercial Aircraft Deliveries
en.summary: Airbus reported a strong financial performance for the second quarter and first half of 2026. Driven by a surge in commercial aircraft deliveries to 237 units in Q2, the manufacturer's quarterly net income jumped 126% to $1.66 billion (€1.65 billion). For the first half of 2026, Airbus delivered 351 commercial aircraft and generated consolidated revenues of €33.2 billion. The European aerospace giant maintained its full-year guidance to deliver approximately 870 commercial aircraft and achieved a commercial order backlog of 9,222 planes by the end of June, while continuing to ramp up its passenger jet production rates across several programs.
body: According to reports from AeroTime and official disclosures from Airbus, the European aircraft manufacturer published its consolidated financial results for the first half of 2026 on July 29, 2026. The financial data highlights a significant surge in the second quarter of the year, driven by robust commercial aircraft deliveries. Airbus' quarterly net income grew by 126% to $1.66 billion (€1.65 billion), up from $842 million (€732 million) recorded during the same period last year, while Q2 revenue increased by 28% year-on-year.

In terms of operational output, Airbus delivered 237 commercial aircraft to customers between April and June 2026, marking a substantial recovery from the 114 aircraft delivered in the first quarter between January and March. This brought the total deliveries for the first half of 2026 to 351 aircraft, up from 306 deliveries in H1 2025. The H1 deliveries comprised 44 A220s, 271 A320 Family aircraft, 10 A330s, and 26 A350s.

For the first six months of 2026, Airbus reported consolidated revenues of €33.2 billion ($38.2 billion), representing a 12% increase compared to €29.6 billion in H1 2025. Consolidated EBIT Adjusted, a key metric of underlying business performance, reached €2,727 million, up from €2,204 million in the prior-year period. CEO Guillaume Faury noted that the positive results primarily reflect higher commercial aircraft deliveries and strong performance within the Defense and Space division.

The company also experienced strong commercial momentum, recording 886 gross commercial orders during the first half of 2026, compared to 494 gross orders in the same period last year. Net commercial orders after cancellations stood at 821 aircraft. By the end of June 2026, the manufacturer's total commercial aircraft order backlog reached 9,222 planes, highlighting sustained market demand.

Looking ahead, Airbus has maintained its full-year delivery guidance of approximately 870 commercial aircraft for 2026. The company also expects its full-year EBIT Adjusted to reach €7.5 billion ($8.6 billion) by year-end. Meanwhile, Airbus continues to advance its aircraft production ramp-up targets, which include reaching a monthly production rate of 13 for the A220 in 2028, between 70 and 75 for the A320 family by the end of 2027, 5 for the A330 program in 2029, and 12 for the A350 program in 2028.

facts.claim: Q2 2026 Airbus net income rose 126% to $1.66 billion (€1.65 billion) from $842 million (€732 million) in the same period last year, alongside a 28% increase in Q2 revenue.
facts.sourceQuote: Net income increased from $842 million (€732 million) to $1.66 billion (€1.65 billion) in Q2 2026 while revenue rose 28% over the same period.

facts.claim: In the first half of 2026, Airbus delivered 351 commercial aircraft, up from 306 in H1 2025, including 237 delivered in the second quarter compared to 114 in the first quarter.
facts.sourceQuote: Between April and June 2026, Airbus delivered 237 commercial aircraft to customers while between January and March 2026, just 114 were delivered. The total for 2026 first half stands at 351.

facts.claim: Airbus reported consolidated revenues of €33.2 billion ($38.2 billion) for H1 2026, a 12% increase year-on-year, with a consolidated EBIT Adjusted of €2.77 billion (€2,727 million).
facts.sourceQuote: Consolidated revenues increased 12% year-on-year to € 33.2 billion (H1 2025: € 29.6 billion).

facts.claim: Commercial aircraft gross orders reached 886 units (821 net orders) in the first half of 2026, bringing the total order backlog to 9,222 commercial aircraft at the end of June 2026.
facts.sourceQuote: Gross commercial aircraft orders totalled 886 (H1 2025: 494 aircraft) with net orders of 821 aircraft after cancellations (H1 2025: 402 aircraft). The order backlog amounted to 9,222
